newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish pasta maker imports durum, buying more.
newsitem.headline: Turkish pasta maker imports durum, buying more.

text.p: Turkish pasta producer Filiz Makarna said on Wednesday it was importing 18,000 tonnes of durum wheat and would import up to 15,000 tonnes more this year.

"We have imported a total of 38,000 tonnes this year including the 18,000 tonnes. We need imported durum as good local durum wheat was purchased by the (state) grain board (TMO)," said Murat Bozkurt, a company official.
He did not disclose the origin of the imports.
He said Italian pasta maker Barilla had recently bought 55 percent of Filiz, one of the leading pasta producers in Turkey.
"We cannot use lower quality durum wheat from domestic crop and our new partner is very keen on using imported durum. So we will import maybe 15,000 tonnes more wheat," he told Reuters.

He said the imports would be carried out despite a government decree on Saturday which raised import taxes on wheat and corn imports to 15 percent from three percent to encourage use of domestic output.
TMO officials said they had purchased about 450,000 tonnes of durum wheat from local producers so far this year at subsidised prices.
Another pasta producer said earlier it would soon import 40,000 tonnes of durum in two cargoes for October and November delivery.
